## The bug

`ArticleController.create()` is the only handler that returns a bare entity instead of the response envelope.

`src/article/article.service.ts:170` — note the return type and the final line:

```ts
async create(userId: number, articleData: CreateArticleDto): Promise<ArticleEntity> {
  ...
  const newArticle = await this.articleRepository.save(article);
  ...
  return newArticle;   // ← bare ArticleEntity
}
```

Every other endpoint returns `ArticleRO`, i.e. `{ article }` — `findOne()` at `article.service.ts:96` does `return {article}`, as do `update()`, `favorite()`, `addComment()`, etc. So `POST /articles` responds with:

```json
{ "slug": "how-to-train-your-dragon-4f2k1c", "title": "...", ... }
```

when the RealWorld spec (and every RealWorld frontend) expects:

```json
{ "article": { "slug": "...", ... } }
```

The React client does `response.article.slug` to redirect to the new article's page → `article` is `undefined` → **"Cannot read property 'slug' of undefined"**.

**Why the server logs nothing:** nothing failed server-side. The row was written, the response was `201`, the request completed normally. The crash is entirely in the browser, one property access past a successful response. The article you "failed" to create is actually in the database — reload the article list and it's there.

This is a known regression on this codebase, already recorded in `LESSONS.md:49` (upstream issue #57), with the rule: *a handler whose return type is not a `*RO` interface is a bug even if it "works" in Postman.*

## The fix

```ts
// article.service.ts
async create(userId: number, articleData: CreateArticleDto): Promise<ArticleRO> {
  ...
  const article = await this.articleRepository.save(newArticle);
  ...
  return { article };
}
```

`ArticleRO` is already imported at `article.service.ts:10`, and the controller just passes the value through, so nothing else needs to change.

## Two things you'll hit next, in the same method

Worth fixing in the same pass, since the frontend will break on them right after:

1. **`body` is never assigned.** `create()` sets `title`, `description`, `slug`, `tagList`, `comments` — but not `article.body = articleData.body`. The column defaults to `''` (`article.entity.ts:20`), so every created article saves with an empty body and the article page renders blank.
2. **`author` is missing from the response.** The returned entity comes from `save()` before the author relation is attached, and `author` isn't eager (`schema.md:42`). RealWorld clients read `article.author.username` to render the byline — that's the same crash shape, one step later. Re-read the article with `relations: ['author']` before returning, or assign `article.author = author` prior to the save.

Want me to apply all three?
